title: Finite Field Realisation of the Classical Constants π and e

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed shell $\Fp(\tau;0,1,\gen)$ of capacity $\kap$, $\p=4\kap+1$, with its phase cycle $\PhiP\cong C_{\p-1}$, the oriented quarter-turn $\im=\gen^{-\kap}$ and the conjugate chirality; the framed rationals $\fQ$ with the shell reading $\rep{\cdot}$; the finitist position that the discrete register is primary.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Transcendence and irrationality of the classical values: Hermite for $\eR$, Lindemann for $\piR$, Niven's irrationality proof --- statements about the continuum register, used here only in Lemma~\ref{lem:norad}.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The classical prime congruences: Wilson, Fermat, Kummer's carry criterion, Lucas, Wolstenholme, Morley, Lerch, and Gauss's central-binomial congruence $\Cb{\kap}\equiv2a\pmod\p$ with its normalisation.

rows.label: A4

rows.label: A5

rows.label: A6

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: Equidistribution of $\lambda(\im)/\p$ over the primes $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec), read on the shells of the totality as the uniform model: the sole import behind the frequency of calibrated shells (H4) and the generic-growth reading of the heights (J3).

rows.label: A8

rows.label: B1

rows.label: B2

rows.label: B4

This is the statement of record superseding the framed-real construction of \cite{akhtman2025algebra}, \S4.4.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The registration quotient: at grade $n$ the observer forgets phase labels and cycle type, tallies all reversible relabellings of $n$ marks with unit weight, and retains only the coincidence predicate. The first of the paper's two \tD{} moves; not implied by cyclicity (the cyclic shifts alone give $n-1$ fixed-point-free relabellings).

rows.label: C2

rows.predicate: The Cayley quarter-turn map $C(x)=(1+\im x)/(1-\im x)$ on $\Fp$ (denominators units): $C(0)=1$, $C(1)=\im$, and $C(x)C(y)=C\bigl((x+y)/(1-xy)\bigr)$, the rational composition law being the half-angle form of phase composition; shell arithmetic only.

rows.label: C4

The second and last \tD{} move.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The joint-return tally: with $C_n=\Cb{n}$ the returning $\pm1$ histories of length $2n$ in one direction, the paired histories in the directions $1$ and $\im$ number $16^{n}$ and the joint returns $C_n^{2}$, and $\piR=\lim16^{n}/(nC_n^{2})$ by the Wallis bounds (E2).

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The tail form: $\dr{n}=n!/\eR+(-1)^{n}\delta_n$ with $\delta_n\in(1/(n+2),1/(n+1))$, so $\dr{n}$ is the nearest integer to $n!/\eR$.

rows.label: D3

blocks.title: The frame-internal life of $e$: the residue line and the Kurepa wall

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: Wilson reflection: for an odd prime $\p$ and $0\le k\le\p-1$, $1/k!\equiv-(-1)^{k}(\p-1-k)!\pmod\p$.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The wall identity and the terminal residue of $e$: $\dr{(\p-1)}\equiv\Ku{\p}\pmod\p$ (the odd-prime case of the Mijajlovi\'c--\v Sami congruence, A4), hence $\rep{\varepsilon_{\p-1}}=-(\Ku{\p})^{-1}$ whenever $\p\nmid\Ku{\p}$; existence of the terminal link on a shell is equivalent to $\p\nmid\Ku{\p}$, universal existence over the shells of the totality to the vanishing of Kurepa's certificate (Z1); re-verified in the derangement form for all $121{,}126$ odd primes $\p<1.6\times10^{6}$ with zero failures of either condition. Beyond the wall $n!\equiv0$: $n=\p-1$ is the factorial horizon.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: Antiperiodicity: $\dr{(n+\p)}\equiv-\dr{n}\pmod\p$ for every odd prime $\p$ and every $n\ge0$ of the totality, so $\dr{n}\bmod\p$ depends on $n\bmod2\p$; the blind set $Z_0(\p)=\{n<\p:\dr{n}\equiv0\}$ always contains $1$, and Kurepa's hypothesis is $\p-1\notin Z_0(\p)$ for every odd prime $\p$ of the totality.

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: Series duals at the wall: $\sum_{k<\p}(-1)^{k}/k!\equiv-\Ku{\p}$ and $\sum_{k<\p}1/k!\equiv-A(\p)$, $A(\p)$ the alternating factorial sum; the group law $\exp(1)\exp(-1)=1$ does not survive, $\Ku{\p}A(\p)\equiv3,0,21,28,132,258$ at $\p=7,13,29,101,257,1009$; on $\p=13$ the direct series residue vanishes ($A(13)\equiv0$) while the derangement side survives ($\Ku{13}\equiv10$) --- a second ground for the canonicity of D5.

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: Blind-scale statistics: over the $501$ primes in $(1000,5000)$ the sizes $|Z_0(\p)|$ distribute as $1^{(169)},2^{(209)},3^{(92)},4^{(22)},5^{(6)},6^{(2)},7^{(1)}$, mean $1.996$, the excess over the forced $n=1$ matching Poisson$(1)$ \apx{} (the model: $\dr{n}\bmod\p$ uniform for $2\le n\le\p-2$, the wall excluded; extended to the $1593$ primes in $(5000,20000)$: $1^{(597)},2^{(569)},3^{(299)},4^{(108)},5^{(17)},6^{(3)}$, mean $1.988$); blind scales never obstruct the plateau of D4 (advance at most $|Z_0(\p)|$ steps past $n_1$). The counts are exact; the Poisson reading is the model they match.

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: The $\p=13$ picture: the residue line $\rep{\varepsilon_n}$, $n=2,\dots,12$, is $2,3,7,11,1,6,\text{blind},2,8,10,9$ --- blind at $n=8$ ($\dr{8}=14833=13\cdot1141$) and terminating on $\rep{\varepsilon_{12}}=-(\Ku{13})^{-1}=9$, the common reading of $6/5$ and $11/7$ --- while the metric row freezes onto $2.71828\ldots$ by $n\approx9$: the thesis in miniature.

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: The fixed-shell tower of $e$: with $\delta_m=\ctr{(-1)^{m}\eP}$ and $q_m=((m\p)!+\delta_m)/\dr{(m\p)}$, $\rep{q_m}=\eP$ exactly at every grade (since $(m\p)!\equiv0$ and $\dr{(m\p)}\equiv(-1)^{m}$ by F3) while $q_m\to\eR$ with the certificate $|q_m-\eR|<(m\p)!/(\dr{(m\p)}\dr{(m\p+1)})+2\kap/\dr{(m\p)}$; on $\p=13$, $q_2$ differs from $\eR$ by $3.98\times10^{-26}$ and every member reads $6$. Compatibility, not selection.

rows.label: F8
rows.predicate: The tail identity: $j!\,\dr{(\p-1-j)}\equiv(-1)^{j}\bigl(\Ku{\p}-\Ku{j}\bigr)\pmod\p$ for $0\le j\le\p-1$ ($j=0$ is F2); hence $n\in Z_0(\p)$ iff $\Ku{(\p-1-n)}\equiv\Ku{\p}$: the blind set counts the collisions of the partial sums of the left factorial with their total, $n=1$ is the forced collision $\Ku{(\p-2)}\equiv\Ku{\p}$, and Kurepa's hypothesis is the return-to-origin question of the walk with steps $j!$.

blocks.title: The frame-internal life of $\pi$: the wall hierarchy

rows.label: G1
rows.predicate: The legibility window: with $m=(\p-1)/2$, $\p\nmid\Cb{n}$ for $1\le n\le m$ and $\p\mid\Cb{n}$ for $m<n<\p$ (Kummer, A3): the residue line of the Wallis chain is defined on exactly $[1,m]$, blind-free below the wall and totally blind on $(m,\p)$; on a frame shell the last legible scale $n=2\kap$ is the angular address of $-1$.

rows.label: G2
rows.predicate: The half-wall terminus, the calibration face: $\rep{w_m}=m^{-1}=\piA^{-1}=4\piA\equiv-2$ for every odd prime of the totality, the return statistics trivialising at the wall ($16^{m}\equiv1$, $\Cb{m}^{2}\equiv1$) and exposing the naked inverse scale; the identities are the calibration web of $2\piA\equiv-1$, and $\rep{w_{\piA}}\piA\equiv1\iff(4\kap)^{2}\equiv1$; the lower chain is blind at the wall and nowhere below.

rows.label: G3
rows.predicate: The quarter-wall two-squares invariant: for $\p\equiv1\pmod4$, $\p=a^{2}+b^{2}$ with $a$ odd, $a\equiv1\pmod4$, at the quarter scale $n=\kap$ (the address of $\im$) $\rep{w_\kap}=\kap^{-1}(2a)^{-2}=-(a^{2})^{-1}=(b^{2})^{-1}$, by Gauss's congruence (A3) with $\kap\equiv-4^{-1}$; the invariant exists precisely under the frame condition; verified for all $211$ primes $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ below $3000$.

rows.label: G4
rows.predicate: Second order at the half wall: $w_m\equiv-2+2\p(q_\p(4)-1)\pmod{\p^{2}}$ with $q_\p(4)\equiv2q_\p(2)$, exact to $\p^{3}$ through Morley (A3). The universal $-2$ persists to $\p^{2}$ exactly for the $\pi$-Wieferich primes (G10): $5$ and $45827$ below $1.08\times10^{11}$ \cite{oeisA355959} and below $2^{35}$ (the package's recorded search); $45827\equiv3\pmod4$, so $\p=5$ is the only Subject shell among them. The normalised quotients equidistribute empirically \apx.

rows.label: G5
rows.predicate: Lucas revivals and self-similarity: beyond the wall $n\ge\p$ is legible for $w$ precisely when every base-$\p$ digit of $n$ is at most $m$ and $\p\nmid n$ (on $\p=13$ the two-digit revivals number $(2\kap)^{2}=36$); on revival scales $\Cb{n}$ factorises digitwise (Lucas, A3); at the first revival $\rep{v_\p}\equiv8$ universally and $v_\p\equiv8+16\p(2q_\p(2)-1)\pmod{\p^{2}}$ by Wolstenholme.

rows.label: G6
rows.predicate: First-order wall vanishing of the arcsin chain: $\sigma_\p=\sum_{k<m}\Cb{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})\equiv0\pmod\p$ for every prime $\p\ge5$ of the totality, $\sigma_3=1$ the sole exception; proved entirely in finite arithmetic through the key identity $A+B=2L$ (coefficient bookkeeping of the formal antiderivative of $(1-s^{2})^{m}$), Wilson reflection, Lerch's congruence and the binomial transfer $\Cb{k}\equiv(-4)^{k}\binom mk$. Verified for all $428$ odd primes $5\le\p<3000$; the ingredients for $m\le60$, $\p<500$.

rows.label: G7
rows.predicate: Second and third order at the arcsin wall: $\sigma_\p\equiv0\pmod{\p^{2}}$ is Sun's theorem (A5), re-verified for $5\le\p<300$; the blind-range sum $\sum_{m<k<\p}\Cb{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})\equiv\p E_{\p-3}/3\pmod{\p^{2}}$ (A5), re-verified for $5\le\p<80$; at third order $\sigma_\p/\p^{2}\equiv(-1)^{(\p+1)/2}B_{\p-3}/36\pmod\p$ for all $1227$ primes $5\le\p<10^{4}$, the mod-$\p^{3}$ reading of Sun's Conjecture 5.1 with the Wolstenholme refinement, a theorem for every prime $\p\ge5$ of the totality (A8): Wolstenholme-trivial at orders $\p,\p^{2}$, Bernoulli at $\p^{3}$, the Euler content beyond the wall.

rows.label: G8
rows.predicate: The $\p=13$ picture for $\pi$: $\kap=3$, wall at $n=6$; the residue line $\rep{w_n}$, $n=1,\dots,6$, is $4,5,10,9,6,11$ with $\rep{w_6}=11\equiv-2$ the calibration face and $\rep{w_3}=10\equiv-(3^{2})^{-1}$ encoding $13=3^{2}+2^{2}$; empty blind set below the wall, total blindness for $n=7,\dots,12$, first revival $\rep{v_{13}}=8$.

rows.label: G9
rows.predicate: The fixed-shell tower of $\pi$: for $n=\p^{r}$, with $\delta_\p=\ctr{\piA B_n-A_n}=\ctr{-34}$, the member $\widehat\pi_{\p,r}=(2\cdot16^{\p^{r}}+\delta_\p)/((2\p^{r}+1)\Cb{\p^{r}}^{2})$ reads $\rep{\widehat\pi_{\p,r}}=\piA$ exactly for every $r$ (Lucas and Fermat give $\Cb{n}\equiv2$, $16^{n}\equiv16$, $B_n\equiv4$) while converging externally to $\piR$; on $\p=13$, $\delta_{13}=5$.

rows.label: G10
rows.predicate: The $\pi$-Wieferich condition in three forms: $4^{\p-1}\equiv1+\p\pmod{\p^{2}}$ iff $q_\p(4)\equiv1$ iff $2q_\p(2)\equiv1\pmod\p$, with $q_\p(4)=2q_\p(2)+\p\,q_\p(2)^{2}$ exactly; Eisenstein's $2q_\p(2)\equiv-H_{(\p-1)/2}\pmod\p$ ($H_m=\sum_{j\le m}1/j$) makes it $H_{(\p-1)/2}\equiv-1$, and $(\p+2)^{\p-1}\equiv1\pmod{\p^{2}}$ identifies it with OEIS A355959 \cite{oeisA355959}.

rows.label: H1
rows.predicate: The frame character $\chi(\gen^{n})=\exp(2\piR\imR\,n/(\p-1))$, the canonical external dictionary sending $\gen$ to $\zeta_{\p-1}$; the comparison map, never used to derive either constant.

rows.label: H2
rows.predicate: The exact angular carrier of $\pi$: $\chi(-1)=e^{\imR\piR}$ exactly in every shell, for every generator and either chirality, since $-1=\gen^{(\p-1)/2}$ sits at arc fraction one half --- Euler's identity as the half-turn tautology $\gen^{2\kap}=-1$ under the dictionary, with no calibration and no error term.

rows.label: H3
rows.predicate: Exact calibration of $e$ is impossible: with $\theta=2\piR\lambda(\im)/(\p-1)$ the frame angle of $\eP$, $\theta\ne1$ in every shell ($\theta=1$ would make $\piR$ rational, A2); $\chi(\eP)$ is a root of unity while $e^{\imR}$ is not, so the identification is intrinsically horizon-limited.

rows.label: H4
rows.predicate: Calibrated shells at every fixed precision $\varepsilon\le1$: the $\varepsilon$-calibrated shells have asymptotic density $2\varepsilon/\piR$ among the shells $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (A7), so large enough ranges hold them, $\chi(\eP)$ within $\varepsilon$ of $e^{\imR}$ there; the uniform model reads $N$ shells down to the nearest-hit scale $\piR/(2N)$ \apx. Below $10^{6}$: $260$ shells within $0.01$ against $249$ predicted; the best, $\p=778933$, within $4\times10^{-5}$, decided exactly.

rows.label: H5
rows.predicate: The null experiment: whether $\gen^{\lambda(\pm\im)}\equiv-(\Ku{\p})^{-1}$ for some primitive root and either orientation, varied independently, is the index condition $\gcd(s,\p-1)=\gcd(\lambda(\pm\im),\p-1)$; over the $210$ primes $\p\equiv1\pmod4$, $5<\p<3000$, it holds for $94$ against $96.0\pm6.6$ expected under independence ($54$ against $57.9\pm6.2$ with the orientation tied to the generator), the correlation of the two angular addresses $-0.10$ at deviation $\approx0.07$ \apx: no invariant pointwise identification of the angular and radial carriers of $e$.

rows.predicate: The duality: $\pi$ is angular-exact and wall-trivial (tautological carrier, terminus the calibration face $-2$, Fermat quotient one order down, two-squares quarter invariant, empty blind set below the wall, geometric $\fQ$-rate, the series law split Bernoulli/Euler across the wall) and $e$ angular-approximate and wall-wild (calibration impossible, terminus the open Kurepa quantity, no quarter invariant, Poisson blind set, factorial $\fQ$-rate, the group law broken at the wall); each constant exact on the axis where the other is approximate: $\pi$ a structural, $e$ a statistical constant of the finite frame.

rows.label: I4
rows.predicate: CRT stability: under the composite lift to $q=\prod\p_i$ the half-wall invariant of $\pi$ glues to $-2$ modulo every $q$, since $2\piA\equiv-1$ holds in every fibre, while the terminal content of $e$, $(-(\Ku{\p_i})^{-1})_i$, varies fibrewise. The two selectors resolve the $\p=13$ coincidence: the same residue $6$ reaches $\piR$ through C4 and $\eR$ through C1.

rows.label: I5
rows.predicate: The three frame invariants across shells: on the $4783$ shells $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ below $10^{5}$, the triple $(\Ku{\p}/\p,\ q_\p(4)/\p,\ \varphi/\piR)$ --- the wall of $e$ (F2), the wall of $\pi$ at second order (G4), the angular address $\varphi=\arg(a+b\imR)$ of $\p=a^{2}+b^{2}$, $a\equiv1\pmod4$ (G3) --- is exact on each shell ($\p=13$: $10,6,-3+2\imR$; $1093$: $q_\p(4)=0$, the Wieferich prime); means $0.502,0.499,0.499$ and variances $0.0828,0.0831,0.0832$ (uniform: $1/2$, $1/12$), correlations $-0.016,-0.008,+0.010$ ($\sigma=0.0145$), $4\times4\times4$ chi-square $59.6$ on $63$ df, $a/\sqrt\p=\cos\varphi$ arcsine-distributed (mean $0.004$, variance $0.500$) \apx: consistent with independence on the examined range.

rows.label: J1
rows.predicate: The wrap-free window: an entity of the shell is $\p$-hard when it lies beyond the observer's horizon $\sqrt\p$; the accessible smalls are the natural counts below $\sqrt\p$, where sums and products of two accessible counts do not wrap, so primality, parity and order are wrap-invariant there and only there.

rows.label: J2
rows.predicate: Calibration pinning: the half-period satisfies the height-two relation $2\piA+1\equiv0$, the shell calibration $\p=4\kap+1$ itself, so the observer holds an exact short certificate of an entity it never accesses as a tally; the same pinning covers the quarter-turn ($\im^{2}+1\equiv0$) and the residue web of G2; the pin holds on every one of the $500$ shells $\p\le8009$ with $H(\piA)=2$.

rows.label: J3
rows.predicate: The height run: with $H(x)=\min_{a\ge1}\max(a,|\ctr{ax}|)$ in the smallest-primitive-root frame, minimised over the two chiralities, over the $500$ shells $\p\equiv1\pmod4$, $\p\le8009$: $H(\eP)\le2\sqrt\p$ on every shell (the horizon band), median $H(\eP)=0.525\sqrt\p$ \apx, exactly $68$ shells with $H\le10$, and the pin value $2$ on exactly $\{13,1933,4177,5857\}$; for $\eP$ a relation of height at most $h$ holds only on the shells with $H(\eP)\le h$ ($68$ of the $500$ for $h=10$), a share that falls as the shells grow, $H(\eP)$ sitting at the $\sqrt\p$ scale (the generic-growth reading, A7).

rows.label: J4
rows.predicate: A framed transcendental is a $\p$-hard role with no bounded-height defining relation holding across shells; the chart shadow of a $\p$-hard role splits by its certificate --- a role pinned by a bounded-height relation has an exact algebraic shadow ($\im^{2}=-1$ giving $\imR$), while the half-arc and unit-registration roles, fixed by normalisations (C1, C4) with no such relation, have the transcendental shadows $\piR$, $\eR$. Neither external meaning, hardness nor accessibility rides on a residue symbol; roles carry all three.

rows.label: J5
rows.predicate: Universality and the duality as corollary: $\p$-hardness is self-similar, every shell finding its own half-period and drive name beyond its own horizon, so the chart shadows agree across all observers; $\pi$'s half-period is calibration-pinned with a height-two certificate (J2) and its arc role normalisation-fixed, $\eP$ has neither a pinned residue nor a cross-shell certificate and its role is generator-dependent --- structural against statistical is the certification split (I3). The sporadic small-height shells of J3 are the certificate-level face of I4.

rows.label: J6
rows.predicate: Two constants, two walls: both attach their full-resolution shell content to sparse-prime problems (Kurepa non-vanishing for $e$, a prescribed Fermat quotient of Wieferich type for $\pi$); for each shell the bounded observer holds an exact finite certificate and holds no uniform certificate across all shells --- per-instance decidability without a uniform bound, the characteristic shape of statements at the arithmetic horizon; Kurepa's hypothesis is not thereby decided; the frequency of the persistence shells is a range reading (G4), their totality not a predicate of the paper.

B2.name: FRC.Epi.orientation_transport
B2.doc: 13:B2 — orientation transport: under `g' = g^u` with `u` coprime to `p − 1`, `u` is odd, so either `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and the re-derived quarter-turn `−g'^κ` is `−g^κ` (the same chirality), or `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)` and it is `−(−g^κ)` (the conjugate chart); there is no third case.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orientation_class
B2.doc: 2:D5, 6:B3, 13:B2 — the orientation classes: for `g' = g^u`, the quarter-turn `−g'^κ` is `−g^κ` when `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `−(−g^κ)` when `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

B3.name: FRC.Epi.coincidence13
B3.doc: 13:B3 — the `p = 13` coincidence: with `g = 2`, `κ = 3`, the quarter-turn `i = −g^κ = 5`, the exponential unit `e_p = g^{λ(i)} = 2^5 = 6`, the half-period `π_A = 2κ = 6`, and `6` is the reading of `−1/2` (`2·6 = −1`).

C2.name: FRC.Epi.rencontres
C2.doc: 13:C2 — the rencontres identity (the derangement selector, Prop. selector-e): `Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} x^{fix σ} = Σ_{k ≤ n} C(n,k)(n−k)! (x − 1)^k`, `n = card α`, over any commutative ring, by double counting the pairs `(σ, F)` with `F` a set of fixed points of `σ`.

C2.name: FRC.Epi.rencontres_rat
C2.doc: 13:C2 — the ledger's form of the rencontres identity, `P_n(x) = n! Σ_{k ≤ n} (x−1)^k/k!`: the coefficient `C(n,k)(n−k)!` is `n!/k!`.

C2.name: FRC.Epi.rencontres_one
C2.doc: 13:C2 — `P_n(1) = n!`: the normalised kernel `Z_n = P_n/n!` takes the value one at `x = 1`.

C2.name: FRC.Epi.rencontres_zero
C2.doc: 13:C2 — `P_n(0) = !n`: the value at `x = 0` is the number of derangements, so `Z_n(0) = !n/n!` and the unit registration ratio `Z_n(1)/Z_n(0)` is `n!/!n`.

C3.name: FRC.Epi.cayley_values
C3.doc: 13:C3 — `C(0) = 1` and `C(1) = i` for a quarter turn `i` (`i² = −1`) in characteristic `≠ 2`.

C3.name: FRC.Epi.cayley_mul
C3.doc: 13:C3 — the composition law `C(x)·C(y) = C((x + y)/(1 − xy))`: the rational law is the half-angle form of phase composition, with denominators units.

C5.name: FRC.Epi.joint_return_tally
C5.doc: 13:C5 — the returning `±1` histories of length `2n` in one direction (the sets of `n` up-steps among `2n`) number `C(2n,n)`, the paired histories in the two directions `16^n`, and the joint returns `C(2n,n)²`.

C5.name: FRC.Epi.tendsto_wallis_chain
C5.doc: 13:C5 — `π = lim 16^n/(n C_n²)`: the joint-return ratio converges to `π` (Mathlib's Wallis product).

D2.name: FRC.Epi.tailDelta_strict
D2.doc: 13:D2 — the tail form: `!n = n!/e + (−1)^n δ_n` with `δ_n ∈ (1/(n+2), 1/(n+1))` strictly, so `!n` is the nearest integer to `n!/e`.

D2.name: FRC.Epi.numDerangements_eq_tailDelta
D2.doc: 13:D2 — `!n = n!·e⁻¹ + (−1)^n δ_n`, the tail form itself.

D3.name: FRC.Epi.epsChain_enclosure
D3.doc: 13:D3 — the superexponential enclosure `|ε_n − e| ≤ e(e+1)/(n+1)! < 10.2/(n+1)!` for `n ≥ 2`.

D4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_binary64
D4.doc: 13:D4, 13:I1 — `e` lies within the half-ulp `2⁻⁵²` of the binary64 constant (from Mathlib's twenty-digit bracket of `e`), `ε_18` lies within the same half-ulp, and no `ε_n` with `2 ≤ n ≤ 17` does: `n = 18` is the minimal readout grade.

D4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_within_ulp
D4.doc: 13:D4 — the readout within one grid step: for `n ≥ 2` with `e(e+1)/(n+1)! < 2^{−k}` (the threshold `n₀(k)`), `ρ_k(ε_n)` is `ρ_k(e)` or its neighbour, `|ρ_k(ε_n) − ρ_k(e)| ≤ 2^{2−k}`.

D4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_plateau
D4.doc: 13:D4 — the plateau: for `n ≥ 2` with `e(e+1)/(n+1)! < d_k(e)`, the enclosure lies in the rounding cell of `e` and `ρ_k(ε_n) = ρ_k(e)`; the readouts below that index are compared exactly (the package's e.R2).

D4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_six_bits
D4.doc: 13:D4 — the threshold `n₀(k)` alone does not give the plateau: at `k = 6`, `n₀(6) = 5`, `ε₅ = 30/11` reads out as `44/16` and `e` as `43/16`, although `e(e+1)/6! < 2⁻⁶`.

D4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_e_core
D4.doc: 13:D4, 13:I1 — the binary64 readout of `e` in the integers: `ε₁₈ = 18!/!18` lies within the half-ulp of the binary64 constant `6121026514868073/2⁵¹` and no `ε_n` with `2 ≤ n ≤ 17` does; `!18 = 2355301661033953`.

D5.name: FRC.Epi.derangement_cost
D5.doc: 13:D5 — the derangement chain's step counts: `n = 11, 18, 70` are the least `n` with `8/(n+1)! < 2^{−k}` for `k = 24, 53, 333` (the enclosure bound of D3 with the sharper constant `8`; `8/(m+1)!` falls with `m`).

D5.name: FRC.Epi.compound_cost
D5.doc: 13:D5, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the compound chain is slow: `(1 + 1/n)^n ≤ e · 4n/(4n+1)` for `n ≥ 5`, so the gap `e − (1+1/n)^n` is at least `e/(4n+1)`: `k` bits cost `n ≍ 2^k` steps.

D5.name: FRC.Epi.derangement_cost_core
D5.doc: 13:D5, 13:E5 — the step counts of the derangement chain: `n = 11, 18, 70` are the least `n` with `8·2^k < (n+1)!` for `k = 24, 53, 333` (the enclosure bound `8/(n+1)!` below `2^{−k}`), decided in the integers.

E2.name: FRC.Epi.wallis_enclosure
E2.doc: 13:E2, 13:I2 — the two-sided enclosure `v_n < π < w_n` for every `n ≥ 1`: the lower chain is the doubled Wallis partial product `2W_n < 2W_{n+1} ≤ π`, the upper chain is `W_n(2n+1)/n ≥ π(2n+1)²/(4n(n+1)) > π`.

E2.name: FRC.Epi.wallis_width
E2.doc: 13:E2 — the exact width identity `w_n − v_n = w_n/(2n+1)` for `n ≥ 1`.

E2.name: FRC.Epi.wallisV_strictMono
E2.doc: 13:E2 — the Wallis lower chain `v_n` is strictly increasing.

E2.name: FRC.Epi.wallisW_strictAnti
E2.doc: 13:E2 — the Wallis upper chain `w_n` is strictly decreasing from `n = 1`.

E3.name: FRC.Epi.pi_bracket_24
E3.doc: 13:E3 — the rational bracket of `π` at `m = 12`, the ends of the pairing enclosure as reduced fractions (width below `10⁻³⁶`): the bracket on which the core's `arcsin_tail_bound` decides the tail bound of the arcsin chain for `1 ≤ n ≤ 40`.

E3.name: FRC.Epi.arcsin_tail_bound
E3.doc: 13:E3 — the tail bound of the arcsin chain, `|π − s_n| < 4⁻ⁿ/(2n+3)`, holds against the certified bracket of `π` for every `1 ≤ n ≤ 40`.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.machin_bound
E4.doc: 13:E4, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the Machin chain's error: `|M_N − π| < 17/((2N+3)·5^{2N+3})` for every `N`, from Machin's formula `π/4 = 4 arctan(1/5) − arctan(1/239)` and the alternating bound on each arctangent series: the geometric `ℚ`-rate of `π`.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.readout_binary64_pi
E4.doc: 13:E4, 13:I2 — the binary64 readout of `π`: `π` and `M_10` lie within the half-ulp `2⁻⁵²` of the binary64 constant (Mathlib's twenty-digit bracket of `π`), and no `M_N` with `N ≤ 9` does: `N = 10` is minimal.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.machin_hundred_digits
E4.doc: 13:E4 — the first hundred decimal digits are fixed by `M_71`: `|M_71 − π| < 10⁻¹⁰⁰`.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.arctan_pairing
E4.doc: 13:E4 — the alternating pairing of the arctangent series: for `0 ≤ x < 1`, `S_x(2k+1) ≤ arctan x ≤ S_x(2k)`, a certified two-sided enclosure at every truncation.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.machin_pairing
E4.doc: 13:E4 — the alternating pairing of the two arctangent series encloses `π` at every truncation: `machinLo m ≤ π ≤ machinHi m`, a certified two-sided `ℚ`-enclosure.

E4.name: FRC.Epi.gregory_brackets
E4.doc: 13:E4, 13:E5 — the Gregory brackets, the base case of the pairing: `S_{2m} ≤ π/4 ≤ S_{2m+1}`, of width `1/(4m+1)` — the Leibniz chain's `2^k` steps per `k` binary digits.

E5.name: FRC.Epi.rounding_chain
E5.doc: 13:E5 — a factorial-rate chain exists for every real by rounding: `|x − ⌊x·n!⌋/n!| < 1/n!`, so the feasibility split is by kind of chain, not by rate.

E5.name: FRC.Epi.machin_bound
E5.doc: 13:E4, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the Machin chain's error: `|M_N − π| < 17/((2N+3)·5^{2N+3})` for every `N`, from Machin's formula `π/4 = 4 arctan(1/5) − arctan(1/239)` and the alternating bound on each arctangent series: the geometric `ℚ`-rate of `π`.

E5.name: FRC.Epi.gregory_brackets
E5.doc: 13:E4, 13:E5 — the Gregory brackets, the base case of the pairing: `S_{2m} ≤ π/4 ≤ S_{2m+1}`, of width `1/(4m+1)` — the Leibniz chain's `2^k` steps per `k` binary digits.

E5.name: FRC.Epi.compound_cost
E5.doc: 13:D5, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the compound chain is slow: `(1 + 1/n)^n ≤ e · 4n/(4n+1)` for `n ≥ 5`, so the gap `e − (1+1/n)^n` is at least `e/(4n+1)`: `k` bits cost `n ≍ 2^k` steps.

E5.name: FRC.Epi.derangement_cost_core
E5.doc: 13:D5, 13:E5 — the step counts of the derangement chain: `n = 11, 18, 70` are the least `n` with `8·2^k < (n+1)!` for `k = 24, 53, 333` (the enclosure bound `8/(n+1)!` below `2^{−k}`), decided in the integers.

F1.name: FRC.Epi.wilson_reflection_zmod
F1.doc: 13:F1 — Wilson reflection: `1/k! ≡ −(−1)^k (p−1−k)! (mod p)` for `0 ≤ k ≤ p − 1`, from Wilson's theorem `(p−1)! ≡ −1` and `p − j ≡ −j`.

F2.name: FRC.Epi.derangements_wall_zmod
F2.doc: 13:F2, 13:J6 — the wall identity: `!(p−1) ≡ !p (mod p)` for every prime `p` — the derangement number at the wall is Kurepa's left factorial (the odd-prime case of the Mijajlović–Šami congruence), from Wilson reflection.

F2.name: FRC.Epi.terminal_residue
F2.doc: 13:F2 — the terminal residue of `e`: `⟦ε_{p−1}⟧ = (p−1)!/!(p−1) = −(!p)⁻¹`, and the terminal link exists (`!(p−1) ≢ 0`) exactly when `p ∤ !p`.

F2.name: FRC.Epi.terminal13
F2.doc: 13:F2, 13:F6, 13:I1, 13:I3, 13:J6 — the wall of `e` on `𝔽₁₃`: `!12 ≡ !13 ≡ 10`, the terminal residue `⟦ε₁₂⟧ = 9 = −(!13)⁻¹`, the common reading of `6/5` and `11/7`.

F3.name: FRC.Epi.derangements_antiperiodic_zmod
F3.doc: 13:F3 — antiperiodicity: `!(n + p) ≡ −!n (mod p)` for every odd prime `p` and every `n ≥ 0`, so `!n mod p` depends on `n mod 2p`; the blind set always contains `n = 1` (`!1 = 0`).

F3.name: FRC.Epi.dr_antiperiodic
F3.doc: 13:F3, 13:I1 — antiperiodicity on every shell `p = 4κ + 1`: `!(n + p) ≡ −!n (mod p)` for every `n`, so `!n mod p` depends on `n mod 2p`; and the blind set contains `n = 1` (`!1 = 0`).

F3.name: FRC.Epi.dr_succ
F3.doc: 13:F3 — the signed recurrence on the shell: `!(n+1) = (n+1)·!n + (−1)^{n+1}`.

F4.name: FRC.Epi.series_duals_zmod
F4.doc: 13:F4 — the series duals at the wall: `Σ_{k<p} (−1)^k/k! ≡ −!p` and `Σ_{k<p} 1/k! ≡ −A(p)`, `A(p)` the alternating factorial sum, for every odd prime `p`.

F4.name: FRC.Epi.kurepa_alt_values
F4.doc: 13:F4, 13:I3 — the broken group law at the wall: `!p·A(p) ≡ 3, 0, 21, 28, 132, 258` at `p = 7, 13, 29, 101, 257, 1009`, with `A(13) ≡ 0` (the direct series residue vanishes on `𝔽₁₃`).

F5.name: FRC.Epi.blind_census
F5.doc: 13:F5, 13:I1, 13:I3 — the blind-scale census, its opening stretch: on the `43` primes in `(1000, 1300)` the sizes `|Z₀(p)|` are `1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 4, 1, 4, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 2, 3, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 5, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 3` — forty-three exact counts of the Poisson-read distribution (the full census of `501` primes is the package's check of F5).

F6.name: FRC.Epi.residue_line_e13
F6.doc: 13:F6 — the residue line of `e` on `𝔽₁₃`: `⟦ε_n⟧`, `n = 2, …, 12`, is `2, 3, 7, 11, 1, 6, blind, 2, 8, 10, 9` (the blind scale `n = 8` reads `0` here: `!8 = 14833 = 13·1141`).

F6.name: FRC.Epi.terminal13
F6.doc: 13:F2, 13:F6, 13:I1, 13:I3, 13:J6 — the wall of `e` on `𝔽₁₃`: `!12 ≡ !13 ≡ 10`, the terminal residue `⟦ε₁₂⟧ = 9 = −(!13)⁻¹`, the common reading of `6/5` and `11/7`.

F7.name: FRC.Epi.tower_e_exact_zmod
F7.doc: 13:F7 — the fixed-shell tower of `e` is exact at every grade: `(mp)! ≡ 0` and `!(mp) ≡ (−1)^m (mod p)` for `m ≥ 1`, so `q_m = ((mp)! + δ_m)/!(mp)` reads `e_p` on the shell whenever `δ_m ≡ (−1)^m e_p`.

F7.name: FRC.Epi.tower_e_exact
F7.doc: 13:F7 — the fixed-shell tower of `e`, exact at every grade: `(mp)! ≡ 0` and `!(mp) ≡ (−1)^m` for `m ≥ 1`, so the member `q_m = ((mp)! + δ_m)/!(mp)` reads `e_p` — numerator `≡ !(mp)·e_p` — whenever `δ_m ≡ (−1)^m e_p`.

F8.name: FRC.Epi.tail_identity_zmod
F8.doc: 13:F8, 13:Z1 — the tail identity on the shell: `j! · !(p−1−j) ≡ (−1)^j (!p − !j) (mod p)`, `0 ≤ j ≤ p − 1`.

F8.name: FRC.Epi.blind_iff_collision
F8.doc: 13:F8, 13:Z1 — the collision reading of the blind set: for `n ≤ p − 1`, `!n ≡ 0 (mod p)` exactly when the partial sum `!(p−1−n)` of the left factorial collides with `!p`; Kurepa's hypothesis at `p` is the case `n = p − 1`, `!(0) = 0 ≢ !p`; the universal blind scale `n = 1` is `!(p−2) ≡ !p` (the tail `(p−2)! + (p−1)! ≡ 0`).

G1.name: FRC.Epi.legibility_window
G1.doc: 13:G1 — the legibility window: `p ∤ C(2n,n)` for `1 ≤ n ≤ (p−1)/2` and `p ∣ C(2n,n)` for `(p−1)/2 < n < p` — the residue line of the Wallis chain is defined exactly on `[1, (p−1)/2]`.

G1.name: FRC.Epi.residue_line_pi13
G1.doc: 13:G8, 13:G1, 13:I2, 13:I3 — the residue line of `π` on `𝔽₁₃`: `⟦w_n⟧`, `n = 1, …, 6`, is `4, 5, 10, 9, 6, 11`, the calibration face `⟦w₆⟧ = 11 = −2`, the quarter invariant `⟦w₃⟧ = 10 = −(3²)⁻¹`; the legibility window is exactly `1 ≤ n ≤ 6` (`13 ∣ C(2n,n)` for `7 ≤ n ≤ 12`, not for `n ≤ 6`).

G2.name: FRC.Epi.half_wall_terminus
G2.doc: 13:G2 — the half-wall terminus, the calibration face: with `m = (p−1)/2`, `16^m ≡ 1`, `C(2m,m)² ≡ 1`, and `⟦w_m⟧ = m⁻¹ = −2` for every odd prime; the identity `4·π_A ≡ −2` beside it.

G3.name: FRC.Epi.quarter_wall_invariant
G3.doc: 13:G3 — the quarter-wall two-squares invariant: on `p = 4κ + 1 = a² + b²`, given Gauss's congruence `C(2κ,κ) ≡ 2a` (the import A3), `⟦w_κ⟧ = −(a²)⁻¹ = (b²)⁻¹`.

G4.name: FRC.Epi.half_wall_second_order
G4.doc: 13:G4, 13:I2, 13:J6 — the second order at the half wall: with `m = (p−1)/2` and Morley's congruence `C(p−1, m) ≡ (−1)^m 4^{p−1}` taken modulo `p²` (the import A3), `16^m ≡ (−2 + 2p(q_p(4) − 1))·m·C(2m,m)² (mod p²)`, i.e. `w_m ≡ −2 + 2p(q_p(4) − 1)`; the universal `−2` persists to `p²` exactly when `q_p(4) ≡ 1`, the π-Wieferich condition.

G5.name: FRC.Epi.first_revival
G5.doc: 13:G5 — the first revival: `⟦v_p⟧ = 2·16^p/((2p+1)·C(2p,p)²) ≡ 8` on every odd prime shell, by Lucas (`C(2p,p) ≡ 2`), Fermat (`16^p ≡ 16`) and `2p + 1 ≡ 1`.

G5.name: FRC.Epi.choose_two_mul_pow
G5.doc: 13:G5, 13:G9 — Lucas on the tower: `C(2p^r, p^r) ≡ 2 (mod p)` for every `r` (the first revival is `r = 1`).

G5.name: FRC.Epi.revivals13
G5.doc: 13:G5, 13:I2 — the first revival on `𝔽₁₃`: `⟦v₁₃⟧ = 8`, and the two-digit revivals `13 ≤ n < 169` with `13 ∤ C(2n,n)` and `13 ∤ n` number `36 = (2κ)²`.

G6.name: FRC.Epi.sigma_vanishes_all
G6.doc: 13:G6, 13:I2 — first-order wall vanishing of the arcsin chain: `σ_p ≡ 0 (mod p)` on all `428` odd primes `5 ≤ p < 3000` (the enumeration complete), and `σ_3 = 1`.

G7.name: FRC.Epi.sigma_vanishes_mod_sq
G7.doc: 13:G7, 13:I2 — second order at the arcsin wall: `σ_p ≡ 0 (mod p²)` (Sun's theorem) on all `60` primes `5 ≤ p < 300`.

G8.name: FRC.Epi.residue_line_pi13
G8.doc: 13:G8, 13:G1, 13:I2, 13:I3 — the residue line of `π` on `𝔽₁₃`: `⟦w_n⟧`, `n = 1, …, 6`, is `4, 5, 10, 9, 6, 11`, the calibration face `⟦w₆⟧ = 11 = −2`, the quarter invariant `⟦w₃⟧ = 10 = −(3²)⁻¹`; the legibility window is exactly `1 ≤ n ≤ 6` (`13 ∣ C(2n,n)` for `7 ≤ n ≤ 12`, not for `n ≤ 6`).

G9.name: FRC.Epi.tower_pi_exact
G9.doc: 13:G9 — the fixed-shell tower of `π`: for `n = p^r`, `r ≥ 1`, `16^n ≡ 16`, `C(2n,n) ≡ 2` and `2n + 1 ≡ 1`, so `π̂_{p,r} = (2·16^n + δ)/((2n+1)·C(2n,n)²)` reads `π_A = 2κ` exactly, whenever `δ ≡ −34`.

G9.name: FRC.Epi.choose_two_mul_pow
G9.doc: 13:G5, 13:G9 — Lucas on the tower: `C(2p^r, p^r) ≡ 2 (mod p)` for every `r` (the first revival is `r = 1`).

G10.name: FRC.Epi.piWieferich_iff
G10.doc: 13:G10 — the π-Wieferich condition in its three forms: `4^{p−1} ≡ 1 + p (mod p²)` ⟺ `q_p(4) ≡ 1 (mod p)` ⟺ `2·q_p(2) ≡ 1 (mod p)` — a prescribed value of the Fermat quotient of `2`.

G10.name: FRC.Epi.piWieferich_iff_harmonic
G10.doc: 13:G10 — the π-Wieferich condition in harmonic form: `4^{p−1} ≡ 1 + p (mod p²)` exactly when `H_{(p−1)/2} = Σ_{j=1}^{(p−1)/2} 1/j ≡ −1 (mod p)`.

G10.name: FRC.Epi.piWieferich_iff_oeis
G10.doc: 13:G10 — the π-Wieferich set is OEIS A355959: `(p + 2)^{p−1} ≡ 1 (mod p²)` exactly when `2 q_p(2) ≡ 1 (mod p)`, i.e. exactly when `4^{p−1} ≡ 1 + p (mod p²)`.

H2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.half_period
H2.doc: 2:D1, 13:H2, 00:C1 — the half-period: `g^{2κ} = −1` for the drive of every frame (the half-turn tautology behind `χ(−1) = e^{iπ}`).

H3.name: FRC.Epi.calibration_ne_one
H3.doc: 13:H3, 13:I1, 13:I3 — `θ = 2πλ/(p−1) ≠ 1` for every label `λ ≥ 1` and every `p`: `θ = 1` would make `π` rational.

H3.name: FRC.Epi.exp_I_ne_one
H3.doc: 13:H3 — `e^{i n} ≠ 1` for every `n ≥ 1`: `e^{i}` is not a root of unity (while `χ(e_p)` is one).

H3.name: FRC.Epi.no_exact_calibration
H3.doc: 13:H3, 13:I1, 13:I3 — exact calibration is impossible on every shell of the run: with `θ = 2πλ(i)/(p−1)`, no integer `λ` makes `θ = 1` on any of the `500` shells `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `p ≤ 8009`, decided on the certified bracket of `π`.

H4.name: FRC.Epi.calibrated_778933
H4.doc: 13:H4, 13:I1 — the best radian-calibrated shell below `10⁶` (Prop. calib): on `p = 778933`, prime, the residue `123966` is a quarter-turn (`123966² ≡ −1 (mod p)`), and the frame angle `θ = 2π·123966/(p − 1)` it labels lies within `4·10⁻⁵` of one radian and not within `3.9·10⁻⁵` — the calibration inequality decided from the rational bounds `3.141592 < π < 3.141593` of Mathlib, no floating-point value of `π` entering; the count of calibrated shells and the nearest-hit comparison are the package's (`e.A1`).

H4.name: FRC.Epi.calibrated_shell_core
H4.doc: 13:H4 — the shell data of the best calibrated shell below `10⁶`: `778933` is prime, `≡ 1 (mod 4)`, and `123966` is a quarter-turn, `123966² ≡ −1 (mod 778933)` (the angle bound against `π` is the Mathlib witness).

H5.name: FRC.Epi.index_condition_shell
H5.doc: 13:H5 — the null experiment's index condition on the shell: for a primitive root `g` of `ZMod p`, the target `g^s` is `h^l` for some primitive root `h = g^u` (either chirality, `u` coprime to `p − 1`) exactly when `gcd(l, p−1) = gcd(s, p−1)`.

H5.name: FRC.Epi.index_condition
H5.doc: 13:H5 — the index condition: `u·l ≡ s (mod n)` is solvable with `u` coprime to `n` exactly when `gcd(l, n) = gcd(s, n)`.

I1.name: FRC.Epi.readout_binary64
I1.doc: 13:D4, 13:I1 — `e` lies within the half-ulp `2⁻⁵²` of the binary64 constant (from Mathlib's twenty-digit bracket of `e`), `ε_18` lies within the same half-ulp, and no `ε_n` with `2 ≤ n ≤ 17` does: `n = 18` is the minimal readout grade.

I1.name: FRC.Epi.terminal13
I1.doc: 13:F2, 13:F6, 13:I1, 13:I3, 13:J6 — the wall of `e` on `𝔽₁₃`: `!12 ≡ !13 ≡ 10`, the terminal residue `⟦ε₁₂⟧ = 9 = −(!13)⁻¹`, the common reading of `6/5` and `11/7`.

I1.name: FRC.Epi.dr_antiperiodic
I1.doc: 13:F3, 13:I1 — antiperiodicity on every shell `p = 4κ + 1`: `!(n + p) ≡ −!n (mod p)` for every `n`, so `!n mod p` depends on `n mod 2p`; and the blind set contains `n = 1` (`!1 = 0`).

I1.name: FRC.Epi.blind_census
I1.doc: 13:F5, 13:I1, 13:I3 — the blind-scale census, its opening stretch: on the `43` primes in `(1000, 1300)` the sizes `|Z₀(p)|` are `1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 4, 1, 4, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 2, 3, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 5, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 3` — forty-three exact counts of the Poisson-read distribution (the full census of `501` primes is the package's check of F5).

I2.name: FRC.Epi.readout_binary64_pi
I2.doc: 13:E4, 13:I2 — the binary64 readout of `π`: `π` and `M_10` lie within the half-ulp `2⁻⁵²` of the binary64 constant (Mathlib's twenty-digit bracket of `π`), and no `M_N` with `N ≤ 9` does: `N = 10` is minimal.

I2.name: FRC.Epi.wallis_enclosure
I2.doc: 13:E2, 13:I2 — the two-sided enclosure `v_n < π < w_n` for every `n ≥ 1`: the lower chain is the doubled Wallis partial product `2W_n < 2W_{n+1} ≤ π`, the upper chain is `W_n(2n+1)/n ≥ π(2n+1)²/(4n(n+1)) > π`.

I3.doc: 13:H3, 13:I1, 13:I3 — `θ = 2πλ/(p−1) ≠ 1` for every label `λ ≥ 1` and every `p`: `θ = 1` would make `π` rational.

I3.name: FRC.Epi.machin_bound
I3.doc: 13:E4, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the Machin chain's error: `|M_N − π| < 17/((2N+3)·5^{2N+3})` for every `N`, from Machin's formula `π/4 = 4 arctan(1/5) − arctan(1/239)` and the alternating bound on each arctangent series: the geometric `ℚ`-rate of `π`.

I3.name: FRC.Epi.compound_cost
I3.doc: 13:D5, 13:E5, 13:I3 — the compound chain is slow: `(1 + 1/n)^n ≤ e · 4n/(4n+1)` for `n ≥ 5`, so the gap `e − (1+1/n)^n` is at least `e/(4n+1)`: `k` bits cost `n ≍ 2^k` steps.

I3.name: FRC.Epi.residue_line_pi13
I3.doc: 13:G8, 13:G1, 13:I2, 13:I3 — the residue line of `π` on `𝔽₁₃`: `⟦w_n⟧`, `n = 1, …, 6`, is `4, 5, 10, 9, 6, 11`, the calibration face `⟦w₆⟧ = 11 = −2`, the quarter invariant `⟦w₃⟧ = 10 = −(3²)⁻¹`; the legibility window is exactly `1 ≤ n ≤ 6` (`13 ∣ C(2n,n)` for `7 ≤ n ≤ 12`, not for `n ≤ 6`).

I3.name: FRC.Epi.terminal13

I3.name: FRC.Epi.kurepa_alt_values
I3.doc: 13:F4, 13:I3 — the broken group law at the wall: `!p·A(p) ≡ 3, 0, 21, 28, 132, 258` at `p = 7, 13, 29, 101, 257, 1009`, with `A(13) ≡ 0` (the direct series residue vanishes on `𝔽₁₃`).

I4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.two_pi
I4.doc: 00:C1, 13:J2, 13:I4 — the web closes: `2π ≡ −1` on every shell (`4κ = p − 1`): the height-two pinning `2π_A + 1 ≡ 0`, which holds in every fibre of a composite lift.

I5.name: FRC.Epi.invariants_13_1093
I5.doc: 13:I5, 13:J6 — the three frame invariants on their named shells: at `p = 13` the wall of `e` is `!13 ≡ 10`, the Fermat quotient `q₁₃(4) = 6` and the two squares `13 = 3² + 2²`; at `p = 1093` the Fermat quotient vanishes (the Wieferich prime), each an exact certificate of its shell.

J1.name: FRC.Epi.wrap_free
J1.doc: 13:J1 — the wrap-free window: two counts below `√p` (`a·a < p`, `b·b < p`) have a product below `p`, and, for `p ≥ 4`, a sum below `p`: the accessible smalls neither wrap under `+` nor under `×`.

J2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.two_pi
J2.doc: 00:C1, 13:J2, 13:I4 — the web closes: `2π ≡ −1` on every shell (`4κ = p − 1`): the height-two pinning `2π_A + 1 ≡ 0`, which holds in every fibre of a composite lift.

J2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_turn_sq
J2.doc: 1:B3, 2:D2, 13:J2 — the quarter-turn `i = −g^κ` squares to `−1` (the pinning relation `i² + 1 ≡ 0`).

J3.name: FRC.Epi.height_run
J3.doc: 13:J3 — the height run: over the `500` shells `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `p ≤ 8009` (the enumeration complete), `H(e_p) ≤ 2√p` on every shell (the horizon band), exactly `68` shells have `H ≤ 10`, and the pin value `2` is reached on exactly `{13, 1933, 4177, 5857}`.

J5.name: FRC.Epi.pin_contrast
J5.doc: 13:J5 — the certification split: the half-period is pinned by the height-two relation `2π_A + 1 ≡ 0` on every frame shell (J2), while `e_p` reaches the pin value `2` on exactly four of the `500` shells of the run and otherwise sits in the horizon band `H(e_p) ≤ 2√p`: no pinned residue and no cross-shell certificate for `e_p`.

J6.name: FRC.Epi.derangements_wall_zmod
J6.doc: 13:F2, 13:J6 — the wall identity: `!(p−1) ≡ !p (mod p)` for every prime `p` — the derangement number at the wall is Kurepa's left factorial (the odd-prime case of the Mijajlović–Šami congruence), from Wilson reflection.
